classification.difficultyReason: Find positive areas below the x-axis using logarithmic antiderivatives; part b also requires the x-intercept.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=-\frac{1}{x}$, the $x$-axis, $x=1$ and $x=4$.

spec.description: Reciprocal curve below the positive x-axis, with shaded bounded region from x=1 to x=4 and numerical labels above the axis.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graph features remain visible in the student edition. No calculated answer is shown.

answer.worked:
The curve is below the $x$-axis on $1\le x\le4$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_1^4\frac{1}{x}\,dx\\&=[\ln x]_1^4\\&=\ln4\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of the region bounded by $y=\frac{3}{x}-3$, the $x$-axis and $x=3$.

spec.description: Decreasing translated reciprocal curve through (1,0) and (3,-2), with shaded region below the x-axis, vertical boundary x=3 and dashed guides y=-2 and y=-3.
spec.mathematics: y=3/x-3; horizontal asymptote y=-3; bounded region 1<=x<=3, 3/x-3<=y<=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Source intercept, boundary labels and guides remain visible in the student edition. No calculated area is shown.

answer.worked:
At the $x$-intercept, $\frac{3}{x}-3=0$, so $x=1$. The bounded region lies below the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=-\int_1^3\left(\frac{3}{x}-3\right)\,dx\\&=-[3\ln x-3x]_1^3\\&=-[(3\ln3-9)-(-3)]\\&=(6-3\ln3)\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$
